how_to_update: A mentor or clinician can change any 'expected' value (high, medium, low) and set rated_by to their name and rated_on to the date. lib/grading/answer-key.test.ts then holds the engine to their ratings. 'source' names the reference that supports the rating; 'more_sources' lists any other reference the 'why' relies on.

scale.high: The same molecular machinery is broken: one protein through the same mechanism, or the parts of one enzyme or one complex. Findings, study designs or therapies could plausibly transfer.
scale.medium: Related but different biology: one protein broken in a different way (dominant versus biallelic, gain versus loss of function), or different steps of one specific pathway. Some research questions are shared.
scale.low: No shared molecular machinery beyond broad processes; findings and therapies would not transfer.

biology.why: Both are GM2 gangliosidoses: HEXA and HEXB encode the alpha and beta subunits of beta-hexosaminidase A (an alpha-beta heterodimer), so both lose the enzyme that breaks down GM2 ganglioside; Sandhoff disease also loses beta-hexosaminidase B.

Myosin Va (GS1) and melanophilin (GS3) are parts of one complex: melanophilin bridges Rab27a on melanosomes and myosin Va on actin filaments during melanosome transport. A melanophilin defect and a deletion of the tissue-restricted F-exon of MYO5A give the identical hypopigmentation-only form of Griscelli syndrome; GS1 adds a neurological disorder.
One disease continuum: both are a deficiency of glucocerebrosidase from biallelic GBA1 variants; type 2 adds early, rapidly progressive disease of the central nervous system.
Both are tyrosinase (TYR) deficiencies of melanin synthesis: OCA1A with a complete lack of melanin throughout life, OCA1B with some pigment that accumulates over time.

Same gene, different genetic mechanism: Tietz syndrome is fully penetrant autosomal dominant, from a monoallelic missense change in the basic region of MITF; COMMAD comes from biallelic MITF alleles and adds coloboma, microphthalmia and osteopetrosis, beyond what monoallelic MITF mutations cause.

Same gene, opposite effect: Hajdu-Cheney syndrome (acroosteolysis dominant type) comes from truncating variants in the last exon of NOTCH2 that give a stable protein with enhanced NOTCH2 signalling (gain of function); the NOTCH2 variants of Alagille syndrome decrease Notch signalling.

Neighbouring steps of one pathway: galactokinase (GALK1) and galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (GALT) are consecutive enzymes of the Leloir pathway. GALT deficiency is life-threatening in newborns; GALK deficiency mainly causes cataract. A lactose-restricted diet is used for both.

Different steps of one pathway: both are disorders of melanin biosynthesis, but OCA1A lacks tyrosinase while OCA3 lacks tyrosinase-related protein 1, which takes part in eumelanin synthesis and helps keep tyrosinase stable.
Unrelated: gelsolin variants whose cleaved fragments deposit as amyloid, versus a missing enzyme of galactose metabolism.

Unrelated machinery: type II collagen of cartilage and vitreous (COL2A1) versus carbonic anhydrase II, which bone resorption and urinary acidification need (CA2). Reactome places both genes only in a broad developmental pathway of pancreatic duct cells.

Unrelated machinery: the regulatory subunit of PI3 kinase (PIK3R1), whose loss lowers PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling, versus the inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor type 1 (ITPR1) behind a congenital nonprogressive ataxia. Reactome places both only in broad signalling pathways.

Unrelated machinery: a subunit of a lysosomal enzyme (HEXA) versus a truncated decorin that can no longer organise collagen in the corneal stroma (DCN). Reactome lists decorin in chondroitin and dermatan sulfate degradation as a substrate proteoglycan, not as an enzyme.

Unrelated machinery: the beta subunit of beta-hexosaminidase A and B (HEXB), whose loss stops the breakdown of GM2 ganglioside in lysosomes, versus a truncated decorin that can no longer organise collagen in the corneal stroma (DCN). Reactome lists decorin in chondroitin and dermatan sulfate degradation as a substrate proteoglycan, not as an enzyme.

Different machinery in different tissues: Tietz syndrome comes from a monoallelic MITF change that disturbs melanocytes (hypopigmentation and deafness); anophthalmia-esophageal-genital syndrome comes from heterozygous loss of the SOX2 transcription factor in the developing eye and foregut. Reactome links the two genes only as a regulator and its target: SOX2 is a direct MITF-M target in melanoma cells, and SOX2 represses MITF-M in neural crest precursors.
